taxonomyNote: NatureServe's primary name is Harlequin Coralsnake and M. tener (Texas coral snake), formerly a subspecies, is treated as a distinct species.
fieldMarks: Venomous. Red, yellow and black bands with red and yellow bands touching; red bands may be speckled with black.
Black snout followed by a broad yellow band across the head.
Slender, smooth scales in 15 rows; adults usually 51-76 cm.
Nonvenomous mimics (scarlet kingsnake, scarlet snake) have a red snout and red bands touching black.
behavior: Secretive: mostly underground, under leaf litter, logs or stumps; solitary outside breeding.
Mainly diurnal in the north (morning and late afternoon); active all year in Florida, least in winter; males most active March-May.
Eats mainly snakes and limbless lizards, sometimes frogs and rodents.
habitat: Hardwood forest, pine-oak woodland, pine flatwoods and scrub, often on sandy soil; sometimes marsh edges and residential areas.
range: Southeastern North Carolina to southern Florida and west to southeastern Louisiana, disjunctly north to central Alabama.
